subject.title: feat(webui): reintroduce opt-in AI purpose titles for tool calls

question: Should OpenClaw accept a permanent default-off Control UI setting and operator-write RPC that sends bounded tool arguments through the utility-model contract to generate decorative titles?
rationale: The implementation defects are mechanically repairable, but accepting new configuration, protocol, token-spend, provider-egress, and persisted-cache behavior requires maintainer product intent; the protected maintainer label reinforces that boundary.

options.title: Accept the opt-in feature
options.body: Keep it default off, require the context/profile repairs and current-head live proof, then accept the additive config and RPC contract.

options.title: Keep deterministic rendering
options.body: Retain current main's model-free tool rows and decline the additional configuration, spend, egress, cache, and protocol surface.

options.title: Prototype a narrower surface
options.body: Explore purpose labels without committing to a persistent core config and gateway RPC before deciding the permanent product contract.

recommendation.title: Accept the opt-in feature
recommendation.body: Keep it default off, require the context/profile repairs and current-head live proof, then accept the additive config and RPC contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged feature history and linked issue show direct ownership of both the original title behavior and the decision to remove or reintroduce it.
